data_origin: Controlled frozen-score release study. All conclusions are conditional empirical risks under the declared class-conditional transport assumption; no population confidence or realized deployment guarantee is requested.
join_policy: Join the two record sets by their common specimen_id. The label-table id is an identical source-row identity; prediction-table id is a unique candidate/specimen record identity. Source row order is arbitrary. Each candidate must have exactly one prediction per labelled specimen. Code 1 is the positive class.

candidate_availability.unavailable_feature: A retrospective adjudication flag recorded after the target outcome.

threshold_rule: Predict positive iff positive_probability>=threshold. A single candidate and threshold must be frozen for all sites; no site-specific switching or score refitting.

deployment_set.definition: A deployment distribution assigns nonnegative masses q(site,label) to the six site/class cells, summing to one. Site total mass must satisfy site_mass_bounds. Within each site, positive mass divided by its total is constrained by positive_fraction_within_site_bounds. The SUM of positive cell masses must satisfy overall_positive_mass_bounds. All constraints apply JOINTLY; site masses and prevalences cannot be maximized separately.

transport_assumption: For each candidate/threshold/site, use the observed reference panel FALSE-NEGATIVE RATE conditional on reference_label=1 and FALSE-POSITIVE RATE conditional on reference_label=0 as fixed working conditional error probabilities. Deployment can change site/class masses only. All present site/class denominators are positive. Do not use joint error fractions as conditional rates.
selection_policy: First exclude candidates using unavailable prediction-time information. For every remaining candidate and threshold, maximize expected decision cost over the entire joint deployment set. Select the smallest worst-case cost; ties within 1e-9 use lower threshold then lexical candidate ID. Separately choose a naive policy by minimum unweighted per-reference-specimen decision cost among the SAME eligible policies, using the same tie rule.
reporting: Return eligible_candidate_ids; worst_case_cost_by_policy using keys candidate_A@0.35 etc for all and only eligible policies; selected_candidate_id; selected_threshold; selected_policy_worst_case_cost; naive_selected_candidate_id; naive_selected_threshold; and naive_policy_is_robust_optimal. No statistical significance statement is requested. Absolute 1e-7 plus relative 1e-7 accuracy.

research_motivation.scope: Distributionally robust classification motivates evaluating policies under an explicit distribution set. This task neither reproduces the paper dataset nor claims its algorithm.
